findings.title: No re-roll/lock mechanism for Match-of-the-Day — code comment admits it's not built yet, risking a 'slot machine' perception or dead-end UX
findings.detail: `src/lib/v2/match-of-the-day.ts` comment explicitly states: 'Future: добавить match locking — раз в день один и тот же match (через user_daily_match таблицу) чтобы избежать рулетки при F5.' Currently, calling `getMatchOfTheDay` likely re-runs `getRecommendations(viewerId, 1)` fresh each time (no persistence of 'today's pick'), meaning a user refreshing the page could get a different top candidate each time (since scoring order could shift as match_views/interests change), or repeatedly see the same one with no visible state — either way, this is not yet a deterministic 'one editorial recommendation per day' product experience as designed, undermining the core differentiation of the pivot (editorial single-match vs. feed).
findings.evidence: src/lib/v2/match-of-the-day.ts lines 18-19 (explicit 'Future' comment, not yet implemented); no user_daily_match table found in supabase/migrations
findings.recommendation: Implement the daily-lock table before or shortly after 10k launch — this is core to the product's stated differentiation ('1 recommendation + editorial story', not a feed) per the V2 pivot memory. Without it, the experience risks feeling arbitrary/buggy rather than intentional, especially if users notice the candidate changing on refresh.

findings.title: No analytics/funnel instrumentation live to detect any of the above risks in production at 10k scale
findings.detail: The spec defines a full funnel event taxonomy and North Star metric (`verified_mutual_interests_with_chat_started`), plus explicit anti-vanity-metric guidance. The existing code audit confirms this is deferred (SYS-022/024/025/027: 'North Star метрика, funnel-события snake_case, §2.4 формулы, per-role дашборды — аналитика отложена'). This means at 10k-user launch, the team will have no systematic visibility into exactly the failure modes flagged in this report — empty-feed rate, gender balance, onboarding drop-off per screen, verification SLA, mutual-interest-to-chat conversion. Flying blind at 10k scale on a cold-start-sensitive marketplace is itself a business risk: problems will be diagnosed anecdotally/too late rather than caught early via dashboards.
findings.evidence: docs/audit-mvp-vs-spec-2026-07-01.md SYS-022/024/025/027 ('аналитика отложена (Sprint 2-4)'); chat13_system.md §2.1-2.4 defines North Star + funnel formulas none of which appear implemented in src/
findings.recommendation: Before or immediately at 10k launch, implement at minimum the North Star metric query and 3-4 critical funnel counters (onboarding_completion_rate, verification_approval_rate, empty_feed_rate/gender_balance, mutual_to_chat_rate) as simple SQL/admin-panel views even without a full event-tracking pipeline — these are queryable directly from existing tables (users, user_profiles, match_requests, chats) without needing the full analytics build-out, and would materially de-risk the launch by making the problems in this report visible in near-real-time rather than discovered via user complaints.

findings.title: Cron infrastructure (delivery + potential future retention/matching jobs) already known-unreliable — a business-continuity risk for any daily-cadence product mechanic
findings.detail: Per user memory/verified facts, the GitHub Actions cron triggering `/api/cron/tg-outbox` was failing due to free-tier limits. Since the core product mechanic is now daily-cadence (Match-of-the-Day refresh, any future retention pushes, notification delivery), reliability of the cron trigger is a business-critical dependency, not just an ops nit — if the daily match doesn't refresh reliably, or notifications silently stop firing, users experience an apparently broken/stale product with no error surfaced to them.
findings.evidence: User memory: baxtlilar_2026-07-01_maestro_findings.md and handoff note GitHub Actions cron was failing (free tier); railway.json config shows single-service Railway hosting with no visible dedicated cron service
findings.recommendation: Move cron triggering off the free-tier GitHub Actions dependency to a paid/reliable scheduler (Railway's own cron, or a paid uptime/cron service) before 10k launch, and add alerting if the cron hasn't fired successfully within its expected window — silent cron failure directly degrades the core Match-of-the-Day experience and notification delivery.

findings.title: Moderation throughput bug (VF-1) turns launch spike into permanently stuck users
findings.detail: The needs_changes -> resubmit path (/api/onboarding/fix/route.ts:58-63) transitions users.verification_status back to pending_review but never creates a verification_cases row (contrast with selfie/route.ts:73-85 which does). Per admin-gap-report VF-1 (critical), this is a normal, common cycle -- many first-time passport photo submissions get rejected for retake -- so at 10k signups this is not an edge case, it is a routine fraction of the funnel. Every affected user inflates the dashboard 'Заявки на проверке' counter (src/app/admin/page.tsx:29-31, counts users.verification_status) but has zero open case, so they appear in neither loadMyQueue nor loadUnassignedQueue (src/lib/admin/load-queue.ts:90-113, both query verification_cases). Result: moderators see a nonzero, growing number with nothing to click on, and the affected users are stuck in pending_review forever with no operator-visible path to a case.
findings.evidence: src/app/api/onboarding/fix/route.ts:58-63 (no case insert) vs src/app/api/onboarding/selfie/route.ts:73-85 (idempotent case insert); src/app/admin/page.tsx:29-31; src/lib/admin/load-queue.ts:90-113; admin-gap-report-2026-07-01.md VF-1/VF-2/VF-3/VF-5
findings.recommendation: Ship the report's proposed fix before launch: single AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE trigger on users WHEN verification_status='pending_review' that idempotently inserts a verification_cases row if none open (NOT EXISTS). This is scoped as one migration (report calls it 'S' effort, P0) and closes VF-1/VF-2/VF-5 simultaneously. Also switch the dashboard counter to count verification_cases WHERE state<>'closed' (VF-3) so the number moderators see matches what they can actually open.

findings.title: No moderator staffing plan exists for verification throughput at 10k users, and per-case work is manual data entry, not a click
findings.detail: Approving a case requires the moderator to manually transcribe 17 passport fields (last_name, first_name, birth_date, gender, citizenship, birth_place, passport_series, passport_number, pinfl, issued_by, issued_at, expires_at, region_code, district_code, locality, street_address -- src/lib/admin/passport-validation.ts:7-24) that then run through validatePassportPayload before admin_approve_verification RPC accepts them (src/app/api/admin/cases/[id]/decision/route.ts:36-60), plus a manual 3-checkbox face-match attestation with no similarity score (FaceMatchStep.tsx:17-48, matches gap-report SG-08). This is real data-entry time (3-8 min/case is a defensible band), not a rubber-stamp. At 10k signups spread over a ~20 working-day launch ramp, that is ~500 verification cases/day; at a 5 min/case midpoint and ~6 productive moderation hours/day, one moderator clears ~72 cases/day, so the queue needs approximately 7 moderators (range: 4 at the fast/3-min end, 11 at the slow/8-min end with rejections and re-checks). If the signup curve is front-loaded (e.g. a marketing push drives 5k signups in week one), daily load doubles and so does the required headcount, or the backlog balloons -- and because of OPS-01 that backlog is partly invisible on the dashboard. No document, config, or staffing plan for this exists anywhere in the repo.
findings.evidence: src/lib/admin/passport-validation.ts:7-24 (17-field payload); src/app/api/admin/cases/[id]/decision/route.ts:36-60; src/components/admin-ops/case/FaceMatchStep.tsx:17-48; admin-gap-report SG-08; no staffing/roster docs found in repo
findings.recommendation: Before opening signups at 10k scale, commit to a concrete moderator roster sized to the actual expected signup curve (not a flat 10k/day-one assumption) -- staff for the ~7-moderator midpoint if the launch ramp is ~3-4 weeks, more if front-loaded. Track actual cases/hour per moderator in week one and re-forecast. Given this is a verify-walled dating app, verification IS the product's critical path -- under-staffing it stalls the entire funnel, not just a support queue.

findings.title: Zero bulk actions anywhere in the admin panel -- every moderation action is one row at a time
findings.detail: Grep for 'bulk' across src/app/admin, src/lib/admin, and src/components/admin-ops returns zero hits. Photo review (PhotosScreen.tsx:30-37) has quickApprove/quickReject per single photo with no multi-select. The verification queue tables (queue/mine/page.tsx:104-206) render one row per case with no checkboxes or batch operations. Reports table (reports/page.tsx) is the same pattern. At 10k users producing up to 30,000 photo-review actions (3 photos/user max, MAX_PHOTOS=3 in src/app/api/onboarding/profile/photo/route.ts:9) and ~10,000 verification cases, single-row-at-a-time operation multiplies moderator click-count and fatigue without any efficiency lever (no select-all-and-approve-clean-batch, no keyboard-driven review flow).
findings.evidence: grep -rn bulk src/app/admin src/lib/admin src/components/admin-ops -> 0 hits; src/app/admin/photos/PhotosScreen.tsx:30-37; src/app/admin/queue/mine/page.tsx:104-206; src/app/api/onboarding/profile/photo/route.ts:9 (MAX_PHOTOS=3)
findings.recommendation: P1: add keyboard-driven single-case review (next/prev + approve/reject hotkeys) to cut per-case time even without true multi-select bulk approve (which is riskier for compliance on identity docs). For low-risk photo review, add real multi-select bulk-approve for the 'clean' cases where no policy flags trip.

findings.title: The only SLA mechanism (7-day stale-case reclaim) has no scheduler wired to it in production -- likely never runs
findings.detail: admin_sla_reclaim_stale_cases (supabase/migrations/20260630010000_verification_case_sla.sql:12-43) is the entire SLA infrastructure per the gap-report (SG-04), and it is only invoked from /api/cron/housekeeping (src/app/api/cron/housekeeping/route.ts). Searching the repo for any scheduler that calls housekeeping finds nothing: railway.json has no cron/schedule field (only build/deploy/healthcheck config), and .github/workflows/ contains exactly one workflow file, cron-tg-outbox.yml, which only POSTs /api/cron/tg-outbox every 5 minutes -- it never calls /api/cron/housekeeping. Per project memory, the tg-outbox GitHub Action itself is already known-broken (private repo free tier exhausted). If housekeeping is likewise unscheduled (or scheduled on the same dead mechanism), cases abandoned by a moderator (vacation, turnover) never get reclaimed -- the report's stated 7-day SLA is fictional in production; those users are stuck indefinitely, not for a week.
findings.evidence: supabase/migrations/20260630010000_verification_case_sla.sql:1-43; src/app/api/cron/housekeeping/route.ts:1-60; railway.json (no cron field); .github/workflows/ contains only cron-tg-outbox.yml; project memory notes GitHub Actions cron already failing on free tier
findings.recommendation: Verify immediately whether anything currently calls /api/cron/housekeeping in production (check Railway logs / external cron-job.org config, since the memory note says this was the suggested alternative to GitHub Actions). If nothing calls it, wire it to a working external scheduler (cron-job.org or Railway's own scheduled service, not GitHub Actions free tier) before launch -- this is cheap (one cron registration) but currently the single point of recovery for abandoned cases at scale.

findings.title: Dashboard has no SLA/due-date/priority surface -- operators cannot see what is overdue (SG-04)
findings.detail: src/app/admin/page.tsx:27-103 is flat StatCards (pending count, photos count, reports count, population, demographics) with no due_at, priority, average moderation time, or 'needs attention' view. There is no per-case age indicator anywhere in the queue UI (queue/mine/page.tsx renders created_at as a raw timestamp, no overdue highlighting). Combined with OPS-04 (the only SLA mechanism likely not scheduled), operators at 10k scale have no way to know which cases are aging past a target SLA until a user complains or the founder manually audits the DB.
findings.evidence: src/app/admin/page.tsx:27-103; src/app/admin/queue/mine/page.tsx:104-206 (no age/overdue styling); admin-gap-report SG-04
findings.recommendation: P1 per report: add due_at/priority columns to verification_cases and reports, surface an overdue-highlighted 'Требуют внимания' section on the dashboard. Medium effort (report estimates M-L), but this is the difference between operators managing the queue proactively vs. reactively at 10k scale.

findings.title: Reports/complaints handling is superadmin-only -- cannot scale by hiring moderators
findings.detail: src/app/admin/reports/page.tsx:65 calls notFound() if session.role !== 'superadmin'. Only two roles exist in the system (role in ('superadmin','moderator'), init_schema.sql:221), so complaint triage is hard-gated to whichever small number of people hold superadmin. Unlike verification (which moderators can be hired to clear), reports handling cannot be scaled horizontally by adding moderator headcount -- it is capped at founder/superadmin bandwidth. The report handling itself is also thin: only 3 status transitions (in_progress/action_taken/not_confirmed, report-actions.tsx:12-15), no assignment, priority, evidence attachment, related-chat view, or escalation (SG-05, high). At 10k users, report volume (fake profiles, harassment, contact-sharing attempts) will scale with population and this is a hard ceiling, not a soft one.
findings.evidence: src/app/admin/reports/page.tsx:63-66; supabase/migrations/20260531000000_init_schema.sql:221 (2-role check constraint); src/components/admin/report-actions.tsx:12-15; admin-gap-report SG-05, SG-01
findings.recommendation: Before 10k launch, either grant a moderator-tier permission to triage reports (requires the RBAC work in SG-01/SG-02, which the report scopes as L-effort P2) or explicitly staff enough superadmins/founders to cover report volume. At minimum, build the /admin/reports/[id] detail view + assignment (P1 per report) so whoever handles reports can work a real queue instead of a flat list with 3 buttons.

findings.title: No 2FA on admin accounts holding passport PII and ban authority
findings.detail: src/app/api/admin/login/route.ts is password-only: verifyPassword() then immediately setAdminSession() (line ~40-61), no second factor. admin_users table (init_schema.sql:218-224) has no TOTP/2FA columns at all. Per gap-report SG-03 (high), a single leaked password grants full access to passport documents, selfies, PINFL, and ban/restrict authority for the entire user base. At 10k users with a moderator team of ~7+ people (per OPS-02), the credential attack surface (phishing, password reuse, shared devices) scales with headcount, and this is exactly the kind of control the parallel MVP legal audit flagged as the top launch risk area (consents/sensitive PII handling).
findings.evidence: src/app/api/admin/login/route.ts (password-only flow); supabase/migrations/20260531000000_init_schema.sql:218-224 (no totp columns); admin-gap-report SG-03
findings.recommendation: Add TOTP-based 2FA before scaling the moderator team past 2-3 trusted people. This is scoped by the report as part of a larger RBAC/staff L-effort item, but 2FA alone (TOTP secret column + verification step in login route) can be shipped independently and cheaply, and should be prioritized ahead of the rest of SG-01/02/03 given the PII exposure.

findings.title: No staff/roles management screen -- admins are provisioned by direct DB INSERT
findings.detail: Per gap-report SG-02 (high), there is no /admin/staff route, no staff API, and admin_users has no status/department/last_activity/invitation columns (init_schema.sql:218-224). Onboarding a new moderator (needed per OPS-02's ~7-person staffing requirement) requires someone to manually run SQL against production to insert a row with a hashed password -- there is no self-service invite flow, no way to deactivate a departing moderator's account from the UI, and no visibility into who is currently staffed or when they last worked a case.
findings.evidence: admin-gap-report SG-02; supabase/migrations/20260531000000_init_schema.sql:218-224 (admin_users has only id/login/role/password_hash/created_at)
findings.recommendation: Build a minimal /admin/staff screen (list, invite via generated temp password, deactivate) before scaling to a 5-10 person moderation team -- doing this via raw SQL for each hire/departure is an operational bottleneck and a security risk (no audit trail for who provisioned an account, no fast revoke path if a moderator's access needs to be pulled).

findings.title: No RBAC granularity -- two hardcoded roles, all-or-nothing access to identity documents and ban power
findings.detail: role in ('superadmin','moderator') is a DB check constraint (init_schema.sql:221), mirrored in session.ts:10 and guard.ts:11. Every permission check in the codebase is a binary superOnly / role !== 'superadmin' branch. There is no way to grant a moderator narrower permissions like 'view identity documents' vs 'download identity documents' vs 'open chat for complaint review' as the spec's 18-role matrix envisions (SG-01, high). Practically, this means every hired moderator gets the same access level as every other moderator, with no least-privilege tiering, and any org growth (e.g. a junior reviewer who should only see photos, not passports) requires code changes, not config.
findings.evidence: supabase/migrations/20260531000000_init_schema.sql:221; src/lib/admin/session.ts:10; src/lib/admin/guard.ts:11; admin-gap-report SG-01
findings.recommendation: P2 per report (L effort -- new tables, permission-guard rework). Not launch-blocking at initial headcount (~7 moderators all doing the same verification job), but plan the RBAC migration before headcount or role diversity grows further, since retrofitting permission granularity onto a live admin_audit_log and guard system is more expensive later.

findings.title: ProfileTab shows only ~15 of the V4 anketa's ~40 fields -- moderators reviewing profiles are missing finance, lifestyle (incl. alcohol/drugs fields), family-model, and the full partner-preference block
findings.detail: Per gap-report §3 (PD-01 through PD-14), ProfileTab's SELECT (ProfileTab.tsx:41-45) never fetches the extended jsonb column, so an entire class of anketa content is invisible in the client card: extended.lifestyle (alcohol_level, drugs_use -- explicitly flagged by the report as 'relevant for moderation' and currently invisible, PD-09 high), extended.finance, family-model fields, and the Big Five quiz vector (quiz_results, PD-13 high, zero grep hits in src/app/admin). At 10k users, if content moderation of anketas (SG-07: no profile-content moderation exists at all -- text/goals are not approval-gated before publishing to Matching) is ever added, or if a moderator needs to sanity-check a report ('this user's profile says X'), they are working from a client card with roughly a third of the actual submitted data.
findings.evidence: src/app/admin/clients/[id]/ProfileTab.tsx:41-45 (narrow SELECT); admin-gap-report §3 PD-01..PD-14, especially PD-09 (alcohol/drugs invisible) and SG-07 (no content moderation gate before publish)
findings.recommendation: P1 per report: rewrite the ProfileTab SELECT+render to include the extended jsonb (one-file fix per the report, M effort) before scaling headcount, since new moderators trained on an incomplete card will develop blind spots that are hard to retrain later. If profile-content moderation (SG-07) is in scope for 10k launch, this is a prerequisite, not optional polish.

findings.title: No content-moderation gate on profile text before it reaches Matching (SG-07)
findings.detail: Per gap-report SG-07 (high): only identity (passport+selfie) verification exists as a gate. Bio text, stated goals, and other free-text anketa fields are not approval-gated before a profile is published into the matching pool -- ProfileTab is entirely read-only (ProfileTab.tsx:80) and there is no 'Анкеты' section in the admin sidebar at all. At 10k users this means any user who passes identity verification can publish arbitrary bio/goals text (contact info attempts are caught by the containsContact regex per VERIFIED FACTS, but non-contact abusive/inappropriate/spam text is not screened) with zero human review before matching begins.
findings.evidence: admin-gap-report SG-07; src/app/admin/clients/[id]/ProfileTab.tsx:80 (read-only)
findings.recommendation: Decide explicitly whether pre-publish content moderation is in scope for 10k launch. If not, at minimum ensure the reports flow (OPS-06) and phrase-based auto-flagging can catch abusive bios post-publish quickly, since there is currently no pre-publish net at all beyond the identity check and the contact-info regex.

findings.title: Single Railway instance with no visible autoscale/replica config + max-5-retry restart policy: a launch signup spike has no headroom
findings.detail: Per VERIFIED FACTS: single Railway service, NIXPACKS, healthcheck /api/health with 120s timeout, restartPolicy ON_FAILURE max 5 retries, no visible autoscale or replica configuration (confirmed directly by reading railway.json, which has only build/deploy/healthcheck keys, no scaling config). Combined with rate limiting that VERIFIED FACTS notes is 'present in a few routes... NOT global,' a marketing-driven launch spike (e.g. a Telegram channel post driving thousands of /start events in a short window) has no autoscale to absorb load and only 5 restart attempts before Railway stops trying, which would take the whole app (including the admin panel moderators depend on) offline simultaneously with the highest-need moment for both onboarding and moderation capacity.
findings.evidence: railway.json (build/deploy keys only, no scale/replica field); VERIFIED FACTS (rate limiting not global, restartPolicy max 5)
findings.recommendation: Before a marketing-driven launch, either throttle the signup funnel intentionally (staged rollout / invite codes, controlling the rate at which /start events arrive) or confirm the Railway plan supports horizontal scaling and configure it explicitly -- do not rely on default single-instance behavior for a spike. Load-test the onboarding path (TG initData verify + start-token consume + bootstrap) at a realistic burst rate before opening broadly.

findings.title: No incident-response/on-call process exists in the repo or docs for admin-panel or moderation outages
findings.detail: No PagerDuty/on-call config, runbook, or escalation doc was found anywhere in src/app/admin, src/lib/admin, or docs/. The only 'incident response' capability referenced in the gap-report is the superadmin unblock-verification path (VF-2, which itself has the same case-creation bug as VF-1) and the two-person ban confirm/cancel dispatcher (guard.ts:128-253, F-119) which is a good control for ban actions specifically but is not a general incident process. There is no alerting on cron failures (the housekeeping/tg-outbox cron silently returns per-task ok:false in JSON with no notification, per housekeeping/route.ts structure), no alert if the admin login throttle triggers en masse (possible credential-stuffing signal), and no defined who-gets-paged-if-the-verification-queue-stops-moving process.
findings.evidence: grep for on-call/runbook/pagerduty across repo and docs/ -- no hits; src/app/api/cron/housekeeping/route.ts returns per-task ok/error in response body only, no external alert wiring; src/lib/admin/guard.ts:128-253 (F-119 two-person ban, the closest thing to a formal process that exists)
findings.recommendation: Before 10k launch, write a minimal runbook (who to page if: verification queue stops moving / cron jobs silently fail / admin login is locked out / a mass-ban or data-exposure incident occurs) and wire at least a basic alert (e.g. a Slack/Telegram webhook) on cron task failures from housekeeping and tg-outbox, since right now those failures are only visible if someone manually checks the JSON response or Railway logs.

findings.title: Photo review queue is a separate, high-volume bottleneck (up to 30,000 review actions) with only single-item quick-approve
findings.detail: Each user can upload up to MAX_PHOTOS=3 (src/app/api/onboarding/profile/photo/route.ts:9), so at 10k users the photo queue can reach ~30,000 individual photo-review actions, larger in raw count than the ~10,000 verification cases. PhotosScreen.tsx offers only per-item quickApprove/quickReject (lines 30-37) with an 'Overdue >24h' filter tab but no bulk approve for clean photos and no visible per-moderator throughput tracking. Even at a fast ~20-30 sec/photo glance-approve rate, 30,000 photos is roughly 170-250 moderator-hours total (~4-6 moderator-weeks at full time), which is a meaningful add-on to the verification staffing in OPS-02, not a rounding error, and currently has to be split across the same 2-role moderator pool with no dedicated tooling to speed it up.
findings.evidence: src/app/api/onboarding/profile/photo/route.ts:9 (MAX_PHOTOS=3); src/app/admin/photos/PhotosScreen.tsx:30-93 (single-item actions only, no bulk)
findings.recommendation: Size staffing to include photo review as its own line item (not folded silently into verification headcount), and prioritize a lightweight bulk-approve or fast-review-mode (e.g. spacebar-to-approve keyboard flow) for photos specifically, since photo review has a much better bulk-safety profile than passport data entry (lower per-item risk, higher volume) and is the cheapest place to buy back moderator time.

findings.title: Admin dashboard queue counters can silently diverge from reality (VF-3) even after the VF-1 trigger fix, if not also fixed
findings.detail: Per gap-report VF-3 (high): the dashboard 'Заявки на проверке' counter and the actual queue use structurally different predicates -- the counter is per-user (users.verification_status='pending_review', page.tsx:29-31) while the queue is per-case/per-assignee (verification_cases state<>'closed', load-queue.ts). Even after the VF-1 trigger closes the immediate case-creation gap, these two counting models can still drift under edge cases (e.g. a user with multiple historical cases, or timing windows around case creation), because they are not reading from the same source of truth. This directly undermines operator trust in the dashboard numbers precisely at the moment (10k scale) when operators most need to trust an at-a-glance signal instead of manually auditing the DB.
findings.evidence: src/app/admin/page.tsx:29-31 (counts users table); src/lib/admin/load-queue.ts:90-113 (counts verification_cases table); admin-gap-report VF-3
findings.recommendation: Implement the report's VF-3 fix alongside VF-1: switch the dashboard counter to COUNT(verification_cases WHERE state<>'closed') so it reads the same source as the queue. Low incremental cost once the VF-1 migration is being written anyway.

blockers.title: Pre-mutual profile page ships exact DOB, marital status, religion & full bio of any target into client payload
blockers.detail: GET /[locale]/v2/profile/[id] builds progressiveData with the target's exact birth_date, marital_status, religion, has_children, future_children_plan, education and full bio, then passes it as a prop to the client component ProgressiveProfile ("use client"). Next.js serializes client-component props into the RSC/HTML payload, so all of that PII is visible in the browser network tab to ANY verified viewer BEFORE mutual consent — even though the UI only renders first name + city + coarse traits. The whole point of 'progressive disclosure' (exact age/DOB hidden until mutual match) is defeated at the wire level. At 10k users this is a bulk-scrapable PII oracle: iterate profile UUIDs (obtained from the feed/recommend endpoint) and harvest DOB+religion+marital status for every published, active user. In the RUz cultural/legal context (serious-dating app, sensitive personal data) exact DOB + religion + marital status of women is exactly the data the product promised to gate.
blockers.evidence: src/app/[locale]/v2/profile/[id]/page.tsx:125-140 (progressiveData includes birth_date, marital_status, religion, bio, has_children); ProfileForMatch type src/lib/v2/match-story.ts:34-38; consumer src/components/v2/ProgressiveProfile.tsx:25 ("use client") renders only firstWord(display_name)/city/traits (lines 108-135) — DOB never displayed but is present in props
blockers.recommendation: Do not pass raw birth_date/marital_status/religion/bio to the pre-mutual client component. On the server, derive only what the UI needs (e.g. an age BUCKET or nothing), strip bio/marital/religion from progressiveData, and send the reveal-level fields only on the isMutual=true branch. Treat every field placed on a client-component prop as publicly readable.

blockers.title: Passport + selfie PII on single unreplicated Railway Volume with no backup/DR — crown-jewel data loss risk
blockers.detail: supabaseAdmin().storage is wired to createStorage() from src/lib/storage/fs-store.ts (a Railway Volume filesystem store), not object storage. All passports and selfies are written to STORAGE_DIR (prod=/data per docs/ARCHITECTURE.md L44) on the single Railway service instance. There is no volume/backup/replica/snapshot config in railway.json and no backup or DR posture documented anywhere in docs/. A Railway Volume is a single-instance, unreplicated disk; if the volume is lost, corrupted, or the service is recreated, every passport+selfie is gone with no recovery path. For a KYC dating app this is the single highest-value asset and the most regulatorily damaging loss. Postgres (native pg on same Railway) has the same undocumented-backup exposure. At 10k users this is thousands of government-ID images with no verified recoverability.
blockers.evidence: src/lib/supabase/admin.ts:4,16 (storage: createStorage()); src/lib/storage/fs-store.ts:1-14; src/lib/uploads/storage.ts:32-34; docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:41-44 (STORAGE_DIR=/data Railway Volume); railway.json (no volume/backup config); grep for backup|snapshot|restore in docs/ returns nothing
blockers.recommendation: Before launch: (1) confirm /data is a persistent mounted Railway Volume, not ephemeral container FS (if ephemeral, redeploys already wipe PII); (2) enable Railway Postgres automated backups + verify a restore; (3) set up scheduled off-site copies of the document volume (encrypted) or migrate document storage to a durable object store (S3/R2) with versioning; (4) document RPO/RTO. Treat as launch-blocking.

blockers.title: No monitoring, alerting, or incident visibility — a breach or outage is invisible
blockers.detail: There is no Sentry, Datadog, OpenTelemetry, Logtail, or any error/alerting integration in package.json or the codebase. Observability is limited to console.error/console.warn lines that go only to Railway's ephemeral stdout. There is no way to detect an ongoing outage, a spike in 401/403/500s, repeated admin-login failures, a volume-fill event, or exfiltration of signed URLs. For a service holding passport+selfie PII, the inability to detect and respond to a security incident is itself a compliance and safety failure. At 10k users, silent degradation (e.g. failed push delivery, DB errors, upload floods) will only surface via user complaints.
blockers.evidence: grep for sentry|datadog|opentelemetry|logtail|alerting|pagerduty in package.json and src/ returns nothing; error handling throughout is console.error only (e.g. src/app/api/health/route.ts:16, src/lib/admin/guard.ts:112, src/app/api/telegram/webhook/route.ts:35)
blockers.recommendation: Add error tracking (Sentry) + uptime/health alerting (cron or Railway health hook to a pager/Telegram ops channel) + alerts on admin-login-throttle events, DB connection failures, and volume disk usage. Minimum: one alert channel wired to /api/health failing and to unhandled errors before launch.

blockers.title: No global rate limiting on a single non-autoscaling instance — trivial DoS via bot /start, API, or upload floods
blockers.detail: Rate limiting is per-route and sparse (admin/login, account, interest, feed/skip, chat, matching quota). There is no global limiter and no Redis/edge limiter. The Telegram webhook fans out to bot handlers with no per-user /start cooldown (grep for rate-limit/throttle/flood in src/lib/telegram returns nothing), so an attacker who obtains the webhook secret — or simply floods legitimate /start via many chats — drives unbounded DB writes. Upload endpoints (onboarding/document, onboarding/selfie, profile/photo) buffer up to 12MB per request fully into memory via await file.arrayBuffer() before any size check, with no per-user upload rate limit. This runs on a single Railway instance with no visible autoscale/replica config and restartPolicyMaxRetries:5 — a sustained flood exhausts memory/CPU, the instance crashes, and after 5 restarts it stays down. Availability of the whole platform hinges on one process.
blockers.evidence: VERIFIED FACT: rate limiting NOT global; railway.json (no replica/autoscale, restartPolicyMaxRetries:5); src/app/api/onboarding/document/route.ts:22 and selfie/route.ts:25 (await file.arrayBuffer() before size check); src/lib/uploads/storage.ts:26,92 (MAX_BYTES check happens after full buffer in memory); grep rate-limit/throttle in src/lib/telegram → none
blockers.recommendation: Add a global IP/user rate limiter at the edge (Railway/Cloudflare WAF rate rules) or middleware-level token bucket; add a per-user /start cooldown in bot handlers; enforce a request body-size cap (reject > ~12MB by Content-Length before buffering) and per-user upload throttle; put the app behind Cloudflare (or Railway's edge protections) for L3/L4 DDoS absorption. Consider raising restart retries / adding a replica.

blockers.title: Admin panel protected only by password + throttle — no 2FA, no IP allowlist, no captcha
blockers.detail: /admin is gated solely by a login form (bx_admin HMAC cookie). Brute-force defense is admin_login_attempts throttling at 5 failures / 15 min per IP and per login — but there is no MFA/2FA, no captcha, and no network-level restriction (grep for captcha/allowlist/IP-restrict in src/lib/admin and proxy.ts returns nothing). The throttle is per trusted-IP, so a distributed attacker rotating IPs faces only the per-login 5/15min limit against a single known admin username — slow but not infeasible over time, and offers no protection if an admin password is phished/reused. This panel can approve/reject verifications and view every user's passport+selfie; it is the highest-value target on the platform.
blockers.evidence: src/app/api/admin/login/route.ts:25 (throttle by ip and loginKey, MAX_FAILS=5/15min per src/lib/admin/throttle.ts:4-5); no captcha/2FA/IP-allowlist anywhere (grep returns nothing); src/proxy.ts:64-70 exempts /api/admin/* from session gate (handled in-route), no network restriction
blockers.recommendation: Add TOTP 2FA for admin login (superadmin mandatory), restrict /admin to an operator IP allowlist or VPN if feasible, and add a captcha after N failures. Given the panel exposes government-ID PII, at minimum ship 2FA before opening to 10k users.

blockers.title: SSE chat stream polls DB every 1.5s per open chat, draining a 10-connection pool
blockers.detail: src/app/api/chats/[id]/stream/route.ts holds an open SSE connection for up to 45s (MAX_MS=45000) and inside the loop polls the DB every TICK_MS=1500ms. Each tick calls loadChatRow (1 query on chats + areBlocked lookup) and getLiveState (chat_messages window query + read_through query) = ~3 round-trips. So a single active chat viewer generates ~2 queries/sec sustained for the whole session. All of this goes through one process-wide pg Pool with max=Number(process.env.PG_POOL_MAX ?? 10) (src/lib/db/pool.ts:27). With even a few hundred concurrent open chats across a single Railway instance (no replica config in railway.json), demand vastly exceeds 10 connections; requests queue behind connectionTimeoutMillis=10000 and then error. This is the first thing to break under realistic concurrency at 10k users — it degrades not just chat but every DB-backed route sharing the pool.
blockers.evidence: src/app/api/chats/[id]/stream/route.ts:9-11 (TICK_MS=1500, MAX_MS=45000, maxDuration=60), :59-82 loop; src/lib/chat/live.ts:31-42,50-87 (3 queries/tick); src/lib/db/pool.ts:27 max=10; railway.json (single service, no replicas)
blockers.recommendation: Move chat live updates off DB-polling: use Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY or a Redis pub/sub fanout so each SSE connection consumes 0 steady-state pool connections, OR raise TICK_MS and cap concurrent SSE per instance. Independently, put PgBouncer (Supabase pooler / Railway PgBouncer) in front so pg pool max can be small per-process while total server-side connections are bounded, and size PG_POOL_MAX explicitly (currently defaulting to 10).

blockers.title: No connection pooler (PgBouncer) — direct pg connections risk exhaustion under concurrency/restarts
blockers.detail: DATABASE_URL points at postgres-8jav.railway.internal:5432 (direct Postgres port, not a 6543 transaction-pooler). Connections are managed only by the in-process pg Pool (max default 10, idleTimeoutMillis 30s). There is no PgBouncer/transaction pooler between the app and Postgres. On a single Railway instance this caps at ~10 backends, but any horizontal scaling, a crash-loop restart (restartPolicyMaxRetries=5), or the cron endpoints running concurrently with web traffic all multiply real backends against a small Postgres max_connections. Combined with DBS-01's polling, the effective ceiling is very low and there is no shared pooler to absorb spikes.
blockers.evidence: .env.access:34 DATABASE_URL=...railway.internal:5432 (direct, no pooler); src/lib/db/pool.ts:20-31 (single Pool, max 10); railway.json restartPolicyMaxRetries=5
blockers.recommendation: Introduce a transaction-mode pooler (PgBouncer / Supabase pooler on port 6543) and point DATABASE_URL at it; keep pg Pool max modest per instance. Verify Postgres max_connections headroom on the Railway plan and document the pool-per-instance × instances math.

blockers.title: No confirmed backup/PITR for the Railway Volume holding passport + selfie + profile PII — volume loss = catastrophic, irrecoverable PII loss
blockers.detail: All identity documents (passport photos, selfies) and profile photos are stored only on the Railway Volume at /data (BUCKET_DOCUMENTS='user-documents', BUCKET_PHOTOS='profile-photos'). There is no code-visible replication or off-box copy — files exist in exactly one place. If the volume is lost, corrupted, or the service is deleted/misconfigured, every user's verification documents and photos are gone with no recovery, and re-verification of the entire base would be required. Railway volume backup/snapshot status cannot be determined from the repo (it is a dashboard setting) — it MUST be confirmed. Given this is legally-sensitive identity data (the MVP audit already flags legal as the top risk domain), running with no verified backup is unacceptable for a real launch. The Postgres DB has the same question (Railway Postgres backup cadence must be confirmed), but DB is more commonly auto-backed-up than a raw volume.
blockers.evidence: src/lib/uploads/storage.ts:6-7 (single buckets on volume); src/lib/storage/fs-store.ts (fs-only, no replication); docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:41-44; premise: RLS disabled on all 30 tables so app is the only guard — data layer has no second line of defense
blockers.recommendation: Before launch: (1) enable/verify Railway volume backups AND set up an independent scheduled off-box copy of /data to object storage (R2/S3) — a nightly rsync/tar job is enough for 10k. (2) Confirm Railway Postgres automated backup cadence + do a test restore. (3) Document RTO/RPO. Do not launch storing passport/selfie PII on a single unbacked volume.

blockers.title: Push delivery reliability hinges on cron that was failing (GitHub Actions free tier) — failed sends may never retry
blockers.detail: Delivery has two paths: best-effort synchronous tryDeliverNow at enqueue time, and the cron-driven processOutboxBatch retry. Per the handoff, the GitHub Actions cron was failing on free tier. If cron is not reliably running, then any message whose synchronous send fails (bot blocked, transient TG error, deploy in progress) is left pending and NEVER retried — it just accumulates last_error/attempts with nothing draining it. The outbox's whole value (retry-safe, not lost on failure) is nullified without a working scheduler. Additionally attempts>=5 rows are silently abandoned (skipped by the drain query) with no alerting.
blockers.evidence: src/lib/v2/tg-outbox-worker.ts:241-268 (tryDeliverNow best-effort; enqueueAndDeliver relies on it), :212-218 (drain skips attempts>=5); handoff: GitHub Actions cron failing on free tier; cron requires external trigger with X-Cron-Secret
blockers.recommendation: Move cron to Railway's native scheduled jobs (or a paid reliable scheduler) and verify it fires on the 30-60s cadence in prod. Add a health metric/alert on pending-outbox depth and on rows stuck at attempts>=5. Confirm both tg-outbox AND housekeeping crons are actually running post-deploy.

blockers.title: Zero monetization mechanism exists — Premium spec is 100% unbuilt
blockers.detail: The premium spec (chat4_premium.md) defines a full tariff model (Free/Plus/Pro/Family/Individual) where the CORE mechanism is: chat only opens after mutual interest AND a paid Plus/Pro subscription (chat_access_enabled gated by subscription_plan). In the actual codebase, chat opens automatically and unconditionally on mutual interest with zero plan check — `src/lib/matching/chat.ts` `ensureChat()` has no subscription/plan gate at all, and `src/app/api/interest/route.ts` calls `enqueueAndDeliver(receiver_id, 'mutual_match')` with no paywall step. There are no `subscription`, `payment`, `tariff`, `plan`, or `billing` tables anywhere in the 50 migration files (verified via grep across all `supabase/migrations/*.sql`); no `subscription_plan`/`chat_access_enabled`/`payment_status` columns exist on any table. `daily_request_quotas` (interests=5/day, views=30/day) is explicitly commented in code as anti-spam only: 'антиспам, защита аудитории — не монетизация' (`src/lib/matching/quota.ts` line 4). No payment SDK (Click/Payme/Uzcard/Humo) appears in package.json or env.ts. This is already flagged in the code-audit doc as SYS-018 (low severity, code-bug framing) — but as a BUSINESS finding it is far more severe: there is no revenue mechanism to launch with at all.
blockers.evidence: grep across supabase/migrations/*.sql for subscription/payment/tariff/plan/billing returns zero hits; src/lib/matching/chat.ts ensureChat() has no plan check; src/lib/matching/quota.ts:4 comment 'не монетизация'; package.json has no payment SDK; docs/audit-mvp-vs-spec-2026-07-01.md SYS-018
blockers.recommendation: Decide explicitly: is 10k-launch a monetization-free growth phase (acceptable IF founder consciously chooses free-for-liquidity strategy) or does it need revenue day one? If revenue is required, minimum viable slice before 10k: (1) DB fields for subscription_plan/status/expiry, (2) gate chat behind Plus using the spec's own can_open_chat() logic, (3) integrate one local provider (Click or Payme) for a single SKU (Plus, 1 month). If NOT required at 10k, explicitly document this as a deliberate 'free growth phase' decision with the founder (per RU-12: don't launch tariffs without terms/refunds/logs) — otherwise the team may believe monetization exists because it's spec'd, and burn runway with zero revenue and no informed decision to have done so.

blockers.title: Cold-start liquidity: strict mutual gender/age-window matching + verification gate = high risk of empty feed at low density
blockers.detail: The `get_recommendations` SQL RPC (supabase/migrations/20260630000000_recommendations_v3_top_life_values.sql) requires BOTH sides to be `verification_status = 'approved'`, `lifecycle_state = 'active'`, profile `status = 'published'`, mutual gender match (`cp.gender = v.looking_for_gender AND v.gender = cp.looking_for_gender`), AND both ages inside each other's declared `partner_age_min/max` window, with a photo. There is no fallback/relaxation when the pool is thin (no widening of age window, no cross-city fallback, no 'best available' degrade). Combined with the Match-of-the-Day model (1 recommendation per day, not a feed) documented in `src/lib/v2/match-of-the-day.ts`, a user with even a moderately narrow preference window in a city with few verified opposite-gender users will hit `null` → the app's own comment says 'UI покажет empty state «алгоритм ищет, заходи позже»' — which was already observed live per user's Maestro findings memory. At 10k total users split ~50/50 across UZ regions/cities with narrow self-selected age windows, most users outside Tashkent will likely see empty state most days, especially early in the ramp before density builds. There's also no anti-imbalance mechanism (spec explicitly calls out gender imbalance risk — 80% male / 20% female — as the 'главный риск' in chat4 §16), and none of the recommended mitigations (extra rec limits, trust-score-gated outbound interest, women's early-access Plus) are implemented.
blockers.evidence: supabase/migrations/20260630000000_recommendations_v3_top_life_values.sql (hard AND filters, no fallback); src/lib/v2/match-of-the-day.ts lines 15-19 ('Возвращает null если кандидатов нет'); chat4_premium.md §16 gender-imbalance risk section with 10 stated mitigations, none implemented in code
blockers.recommendation: Before 10k launch: (1) add a degrade path in get_recommendations — if strict query returns 0 rows, progressively relax age window and city constraint rather than returning nothing; (2) track and dashboard gender_balance and empty-state-rate per city from day one (North Star spec already defines gender_balance metric but analytics is deferred per SYS-022); (3) seed/concentrate initial marketing in 1-2 dense cities (Tashkent) rather than spreading 10k thin nationally; (4) consider a manual/editorial fallback recommendation (admin-curated) when algorithmic pool is empty, to avoid dead-end UX during ramp.

blockers.title: UZ personal-data law risk: RLS disabled + sensitive PD (religion, family, health-adjacent anketa fields) collected without confirmed distinct legal basis
blockers.detail: This is already the single largest finding in the existing legal-focused audit (LEGAL-008, critical: 'Специальные ПД без отдельного правового основания'; LEGAL-006/007/009/011: sensitive-data blocks, photos, and biometric verification collected without separate consent records) — I am not re-deriving these, just flagging the BUSINESS consequence: this is a genuine regulatory risk under Uzbekistan's PD law (biometric/sensitive categories typically require distinct legal basis + consent trail), and a violation discovered post-launch at 10k users (vs. a handful of test users) multiplies exposure — both financial (potential fines) and reputational (a marriage-market audience is trust-sensitive; a PD scandal could be fatal to the brand). Compounding factor for THIS audit's lens: RLS is disabled on all 30 tables, meaning the only technical boundary preventing over-broad data exposure is app-layer code correctness across 34 files — a single missed guard is a data-protection incident, not just a bug.
blockers.evidence: docs/audit-mvp-vs-spec-2026-07-01.md LEGAL-008 (critical), LEGAL-005/006/007/009/015/023 (high); verified facts: RLS disabled on all 30 public tables, RLS is not the security boundary
blockers.recommendation: This is already flagged as P0 in the existing audit's fix plan ('Правовое основание для чувствительных ПД (блокер запуска)') — reiterating here only to connect it explicitly to business risk: do not scale to 10k before legal sign-off on sensitive-PD basis and consent records exist. The cost of fixing this now (schema + consent screens) is trivial compared to the cost of a regulatory complaint or press story once 10k Uzbek families' religion/health/family data is implicated.

blockers.title: No analytics/funnel instrumentation live to detect any of the above risks in production at 10k scale
blockers.detail: The spec defines a full funnel event taxonomy and North Star metric (`verified_mutual_interests_with_chat_started`), plus explicit anti-vanity-metric guidance. The existing code audit confirms this is deferred (SYS-022/024/025/027: 'North Star метрика, funnel-события snake_case, §2.4 формулы, per-role дашборды — аналитика отложена'). This means at 10k-user launch, the team will have no systematic visibility into exactly the failure modes flagged in this report — empty-feed rate, gender balance, onboarding drop-off per screen, verification SLA, mutual-interest-to-chat conversion. Flying blind at 10k scale on a cold-start-sensitive marketplace is itself a business risk: problems will be diagnosed anecdotally/too late rather than caught early via dashboards.
blockers.evidence: docs/audit-mvp-vs-spec-2026-07-01.md SYS-022/024/025/027 ('аналитика отложена (Sprint 2-4)'); chat13_system.md §2.1-2.4 defines North Star + funnel formulas none of which appear implemented in src/
blockers.recommendation: Before or immediately at 10k launch, implement at minimum the North Star metric query and 3-4 critical funnel counters (onboarding_completion_rate, verification_approval_rate, empty_feed_rate/gender_balance, mutual_to_chat_rate) as simple SQL/admin-panel views even without a full event-tracking pipeline — these are queryable directly from existing tables (users, user_profiles, match_requests, chats) without needing the full analytics build-out, and would materially de-risk the launch by making the problems in this report visible in near-real-time rather than discovered via user complaints.

blockers.title: Moderation throughput bug (VF-1) turns launch spike into permanently stuck users
blockers.detail: The needs_changes -> resubmit path (/api/onboarding/fix/route.ts:58-63) transitions users.verification_status back to pending_review but never creates a verification_cases row (contrast with selfie/route.ts:73-85 which does). Per admin-gap-report VF-1 (critical), this is a normal, common cycle -- many first-time passport photo submissions get rejected for retake -- so at 10k signups this is not an edge case, it is a routine fraction of the funnel. Every affected user inflates the dashboard 'Заявки на проверке' counter (src/app/admin/page.tsx:29-31, counts users.verification_status) but has zero open case, so they appear in neither loadMyQueue nor loadUnassignedQueue (src/lib/admin/load-queue.ts:90-113, both query verification_cases). Result: moderators see a nonzero, growing number with nothing to click on, and the affected users are stuck in pending_review forever with no operator-visible path to a case.
blockers.evidence: src/app/api/onboarding/fix/route.ts:58-63 (no case insert) vs src/app/api/onboarding/selfie/route.ts:73-85 (idempotent case insert); src/app/admin/page.tsx:29-31; src/lib/admin/load-queue.ts:90-113; admin-gap-report-2026-07-01.md VF-1/VF-2/VF-3/VF-5
blockers.recommendation: Ship the report's proposed fix before launch: single AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE trigger on users WHEN verification_status='pending_review' that idempotently inserts a verification_cases row if none open (NOT EXISTS). This is scoped as one migration (report calls it 'S' effort, P0) and closes VF-1/VF-2/VF-5 simultaneously. Also switch the dashboard counter to count verification_cases WHERE state<>'closed' (VF-3) so the number moderators see matches what they can actually open.

blockers.title: No moderator staffing plan exists for verification throughput at 10k users, and per-case work is manual data entry, not a click
blockers.detail: Approving a case requires the moderator to manually transcribe 17 passport fields (last_name, first_name, birth_date, gender, citizenship, birth_place, passport_series, passport_number, pinfl, issued_by, issued_at, expires_at, region_code, district_code, locality, street_address -- src/lib/admin/passport-validation.ts:7-24) that then run through validatePassportPayload before admin_approve_verification RPC accepts them (src/app/api/admin/cases/[id]/decision/route.ts:36-60), plus a manual 3-checkbox face-match attestation with no similarity score (FaceMatchStep.tsx:17-48, matches gap-report SG-08). This is real data-entry time (3-8 min/case is a defensible band), not a rubber-stamp. At 10k signups spread over a ~20 working-day launch ramp, that is ~500 verification cases/day; at a 5 min/case midpoint and ~6 productive moderation hours/day, one moderator clears ~72 cases/day, so the queue needs approximately 7 moderators (range: 4 at the fast/3-min end, 11 at the slow/8-min end with rejections and re-checks). If the signup curve is front-loaded (e.g. a marketing push drives 5k signups in week one), daily load doubles and so does the required headcount, or the backlog balloons -- and because of OPS-01 that backlog is partly invisible on the dashboard. No document, config, or staffing plan for this exists anywhere in the repo.
blockers.evidence: src/lib/admin/passport-validation.ts:7-24 (17-field payload); src/app/api/admin/cases/[id]/decision/route.ts:36-60; src/components/admin-ops/case/FaceMatchStep.tsx:17-48; admin-gap-report SG-08; no staffing/roster docs found in repo
blockers.recommendation: Before opening signups at 10k scale, commit to a concrete moderator roster sized to the actual expected signup curve (not a flat 10k/day-one assumption) -- staff for the ~7-moderator midpoint if the launch ramp is ~3-4 weeks, more if front-loaded. Track actual cases/hour per moderator in week one and re-forecast. Given this is a verify-walled dating app, verification IS the product's critical path -- under-staffing it stalls the entire funnel, not just a support queue.

blockers.title: The only SLA mechanism (7-day stale-case reclaim) has no scheduler wired to it in production -- likely never runs
blockers.detail: admin_sla_reclaim_stale_cases (supabase/migrations/20260630010000_verification_case_sla.sql:12-43) is the entire SLA infrastructure per the gap-report (SG-04), and it is only invoked from /api/cron/housekeeping (src/app/api/cron/housekeeping/route.ts). Searching the repo for any scheduler that calls housekeeping finds nothing: railway.json has no cron/schedule field (only build/deploy/healthcheck config), and .github/workflows/ contains exactly one workflow file, cron-tg-outbox.yml, which only POSTs /api/cron/tg-outbox every 5 minutes -- it never calls /api/cron/housekeeping. Per project memory, the tg-outbox GitHub Action itself is already known-broken (private repo free tier exhausted). If housekeeping is likewise unscheduled (or scheduled on the same dead mechanism), cases abandoned by a moderator (vacation, turnover) never get reclaimed -- the report's stated 7-day SLA is fictional in production; those users are stuck indefinitely, not for a week.
blockers.evidence: supabase/migrations/20260630010000_verification_case_sla.sql:1-43; src/app/api/cron/housekeeping/route.ts:1-60; railway.json (no cron field); .github/workflows/ contains only cron-tg-outbox.yml; project memory notes GitHub Actions cron already failing on free tier
blockers.recommendation: Verify immediately whether anything currently calls /api/cron/housekeeping in production (check Railway logs / external cron-job.org config, since the memory note says this was the suggested alternative to GitHub Actions). If nothing calls it, wire it to a working external scheduler (cron-job.org or Railway's own scheduled service, not GitHub Actions free tier) before launch -- this is cheap (one cron registration) but currently the single point of recovery for abandoned cases at scale.

blockers.title: Reports/complaints handling is superadmin-only -- cannot scale by hiring moderators
blockers.detail: src/app/admin/reports/page.tsx:65 calls notFound() if session.role !== 'superadmin'. Only two roles exist in the system (role in ('superadmin','moderator'), init_schema.sql:221), so complaint triage is hard-gated to whichever small number of people hold superadmin. Unlike verification (which moderators can be hired to clear), reports handling cannot be scaled horizontally by adding moderator headcount -- it is capped at founder/superadmin bandwidth. The report handling itself is also thin: only 3 status transitions (in_progress/action_taken/not_confirmed, report-actions.tsx:12-15), no assignment, priority, evidence attachment, related-chat view, or escalation (SG-05, high). At 10k users, report volume (fake profiles, harassment, contact-sharing attempts) will scale with population and this is a hard ceiling, not a soft one.
blockers.evidence: src/app/admin/reports/page.tsx:63-66; supabase/migrations/20260531000000_init_schema.sql:221 (2-role check constraint); src/components/admin/report-actions.tsx:12-15; admin-gap-report SG-05, SG-01
blockers.recommendation: Before 10k launch, either grant a moderator-tier permission to triage reports (requires the RBAC work in SG-01/SG-02, which the report scopes as L-effort P2) or explicitly staff enough superadmins/founders to cover report volume. At minimum, build the /admin/reports/[id] detail view + assignment (P1 per report) so whoever handles reports can work a real queue instead of a flat list with 3 buttons.

blockers.title: No 2FA on admin accounts holding passport PII and ban authority
blockers.detail: src/app/api/admin/login/route.ts is password-only: verifyPassword() then immediately setAdminSession() (line ~40-61), no second factor. admin_users table (init_schema.sql:218-224) has no TOTP/2FA columns at all. Per gap-report SG-03 (high), a single leaked password grants full access to passport documents, selfies, PINFL, and ban/restrict authority for the entire user base. At 10k users with a moderator team of ~7+ people (per OPS-02), the credential attack surface (phishing, password reuse, shared devices) scales with headcount, and this is exactly the kind of control the parallel MVP legal audit flagged as the top launch risk area (consents/sensitive PII handling).
blockers.evidence: src/app/api/admin/login/route.ts (password-only flow); supabase/migrations/20260531000000_init_schema.sql:218-224 (no totp columns); admin-gap-report SG-03
blockers.recommendation: Add TOTP-based 2FA before scaling the moderator team past 2-3 trusted people. This is scoped by the report as part of a larger RBAC/staff L-effort item, but 2FA alone (TOTP secret column + verification step in login route) can be shipped independently and cheaply, and should be prioritized ahead of the rest of SG-01/02/03 given the PII exposure.

blockers.title: Single Railway instance with no visible autoscale/replica config + max-5-retry restart policy: a launch signup spike has no headroom
blockers.detail: Per VERIFIED FACTS: single Railway service, NIXPACKS, healthcheck /api/health with 120s timeout, restartPolicy ON_FAILURE max 5 retries, no visible autoscale or replica configuration (confirmed directly by reading railway.json, which has only build/deploy/healthcheck keys, no scaling config). Combined with rate limiting that VERIFIED FACTS notes is 'present in a few routes... NOT global,' a marketing-driven launch spike (e.g. a Telegram channel post driving thousands of /start events in a short window) has no autoscale to absorb load and only 5 restart attempts before Railway stops trying, which would take the whole app (including the admin panel moderators depend on) offline simultaneously with the highest-need moment for both onboarding and moderation capacity.
blockers.evidence: railway.json (build/deploy keys only, no scale/replica field); VERIFIED FACTS (rate limiting not global, restartPolicy max 5)
blockers.recommendation: Before a marketing-driven launch, either throttle the signup funnel intentionally (staged rollout / invite codes, controlling the rate at which /start events arrive) or confirm the Railway plan supports horizontal scaling and configure it explicitly -- do not rely on default single-instance behavior for a spike. Load-test the onboarding path (TG initData verify + start-token consume + bootstrap) at a realistic burst rate before opening broadly.
